title: How AI visionary Jensen Huang was undone by his own bad decisions
description: Huang always made a point of standing out from the crowd. During the coronavirus lockdowns, he streamed keynote speeches from his kitchen (which gaine
body: Huang always made a point of standing out from the crowd. During the coronavirus lockdowns, he streamed keynote speeches from his kitchen (which gained internet fame in its own right, but were later revealed to have been AI-generated). He is rarely seen without a leather jacket – he has joked that he only owns one suit, and he borrows his daughter's partner's tie.Huang rubbed shoulders with the elite, with a network including Donald Trump, Elon Musk and King Charles. The last time I saw him was at St James' Palace last year, where he was receiving the prestigious Queen's Prize for Engineering. I was told he would not talk to the press - but he wandered over by himself and we spent about 10 minutes having a chat while press officers hovered nervously in the background. He was articulate and optimistic about the progress of AI and the UK's role in it.For many people, Huang was Nvidia. He had as many as 200 people directly reporting to him. He expected high standards – in his book about its inner workings, the Nvidia Way, author Tae Kim wrote the office hours were long.Huang's feedback could be both brutal and public, and he thought nothing of pointing out individuals' mistakes in all-staff meetings. Now it is his own shortcomings which are on very public display, and he has been forced into a brutal ending of his own career.Colette Kress, who takes over for now, will be a familiar face internally and that must feel reassuring to some at Nvidia.She's worked at the company for 13 years and for those who follow its considerable finances, she is often present on earnings calls. She is a billionaire in her own right and a high-flying tech executive.But she's not an engineer and Nvidia's products are highly technical. She will have to convince investors that it is business as usual for Nvidia, that the innovation for which it is renowned can continue at its existing pace, and that the top talent won't leave with Huang.A wobbly Nvidia would be bad news for the entire AI industry because its ever-advancing chips drive the most powerful AI models, and it's also regarded as something of a central bank, loaning money to other firms.As for Huang himself, we assume for now that the investigation into his relationship with the woman accused of being a Chinese spy will continue, and the results of that may well determine what he does next. He probably won't be short of offers despite his conduct – and I expect Nvidia's rivals can't believe their luck that their formidable rival has taken himself out of the game. Elon Musk has already said it would be "an honour" to work with him at SpaceX.It's important though to remember that even if Huang turns out not to have betrayed his company or his country, he still betrayed his wife of 41 years, Lori Huang. And for her, it's not a story of tech, temptation and trillion-dollar-valuations. It's a painfully personal matter.

schema.headline: How AI visionary Jensen Huang was undone by his own bad decisions

title: Russian warship hit by Ukrainian drone in Gulf of Finland
description: Finnish officials have confirmed that a Russian warship was attacked in the Gulf of Finland on Wednesday, although little is known about the strike.Uk
body: Finnish officials have confirmed that a Russian warship was attacked in the Gulf of Finland on Wednesday, although little is known about the strike.Ukraine's SBU security service said it targeted the ship Naro-Fominsk as part of a broader drone operation against Russia's Ust-Luga oil export depot on the Baltic coast.The attack, thought to be the first time Ukrainian drones have attacked a Russian ship in an area of the Baltic Sea open to civilian maritime traffic, has raised questions about whether Ukraine could expand its strikes.Helsinki has been one of Kyiv's closest European allies, and Finnish officials have described the incident as a direct result of Russia's continued full-scale war.Finland's military has given few details of the incident, but it appears to have taken place in a narrow stretch some distance from the Finnish coast.The country's Foreign Minister Elina Valtonen was adamant that the situation in the Baltic Sea remained stable and safe and that there was no threat of any kind to marine traffic. Defence officials are understood to have stressed to Kyiv that the Gulf is a relatively narrow waterway used by oil tankers and civilian vessels, and is also home to subsea data cables.Ukraine's SBU described the Russian ship as a Buyan-M type small corvette that carried Kalibr and Oniks cruise missiles. There were also unconfirmed reports of Russian combat helicopters being destroyed.Martin Herem, the defence minister of Estonia, which borders the Gulf, told public broadcaster ERR that the ship was hit at about 05:30 (03:30 GMT) on Wednesday but did not say how it was attacked: "We know that smoke came from the ship afterwards. The ship itself went back towards St Petersburg."The extent of casualties or damage sustained by the Russian navy ship remains unclear, and Moscow rarely gives such details."The Baltic Sea fleet has been untouched up to this point but there seemingly was a window of opportunity for Ukraine and they understandably tried to use it," said military analyst Emil Kastehelmi, co-founder of the Black Bird monitoring group.Russian and Ukrainian vessels have been repeatedly targeted in the Black Sea since Russia's full-scale invasion began in February 2022, but even though the latest strike on a ship in the Baltic is unprecedented, Kastehelmi told the BBC he did not consider it a serious escalation.Ukrainian drones are regularly launched into Russia from northern Ukraine. Several storage tanks at the Ust-Luga terminal are thought to have been hit overnight on Wednesday and fires at the port were visible over the border in Estonia.Herem said Ukrainian drones attacked the Ust-Luga region from midnight until about 06:00, mostly flying close to the Estonian border but still in Russian airspace. He added that one drone had entered Estonian airspace briefly from Latvia and then headed towards Russia.Nato aircraft based in the Baltic states were in the air at the time, but Herem said it had not been considered safe for them to destroy the drones.Ukrainian foreign ministry spokesman Heorhiy Tykhyy said late on Wednesday that Moscow's allegations that Kyiv had used the airspace of the Baltic states to attack Russia were "baseless", although he acknowledged "incidents might occur when Russia diverts drones from its airspace using electronic warfare".

schema.headline: Russian warship hit by Ukrainian drone in Gulf of Finland

title: 'How does a building just fall?' Neighbours grieve after Brooklyn building collapse
description: Over the loud noise of her radio, Ann Marie did not hear the sound of the Brooklyn building behind her home collapse on Thursday night, but she soon s
body: Over the loud noise of her radio, Ann Marie did not hear the sound of the Brooklyn building behind her home collapse on Thursday night, but she soon saw the flashing lights of fire department trucks rushing to the scene. When she made her way out to the wreckage, workers were still searching for bodies. One of the building's walls had torn off, exposing the inside of several apartment homes, and the rubble had collapsed into a construction site next door. At least eight of her neighbours died in the accident - six adults and two children, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said. "Right now, I'm really scared," Marie told the BBC. "Now that I'm seeing exactly this side of the building, you can imagine the fright of those people, what happened to them."On Thursday afternoon, Mamdani said he had visited survivors in hospital. Eighteen people were injured, including four firefighters. One person is in critical condition.  "I want to take a moment to remember those we have so senselessly lost," Mamdani added. "These were our friends and our neighbours, parents and children, young families building their lives in our city, immigrants from Mexico, Colombia, Trinidad and beyond."

schema.headline: 'How does a building just fall?' Neighbours grieve after Brooklyn building collapse

title: Jesus Owono future undecided following Jesus de Miguel death
description: FC Andorra manager Carles Manso says goalkeeper Jesus Owono is yet to decide whether he will return to football following the death of Tenerife forwar
body: FC Andorra manager Carles Manso says goalkeeper Jesus Owono is yet to decide whether he will return to football following the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel.Owono was sent off after colliding with De Miguel during a Spanish second division match on 2 November, with the Tenerife forward passing away the following day in hospital.Manso said the goalkeeper, 25, is currently spending time with his family and is "completely free to make any decision" with regard to a potential return."What we have to do is support him in every way and be close to ​him," Manso said."We will ​give him space so that he feels completely free to make ‌any ⁠decision, whether he wants to return, when, or if he does not want to return."When he feels it is appropriate and when ​he feels genuinely ready to take a ​decision ⁠like that [he will do so]." Andorra released a statement on behalf of Owono on 4 November, with the  Equatorial Guinea keeper saying he was experiencing "the most difficult days of my life".He added: "I feel enormous pain over the loss of Jesus. I think of him, his family, and everyone who loved him."On Thursday, De Miguel's family released a statement via the Spanish Footballers' Association thanking those who had contributed to a crowdfunding page which has surpassed £170,000.Fran Sol, a forward for Spanish third-tier side Hercules, set up the campaign with all proceeds going to relatives of De Miguel."We would like to express our heartfelt thanks for all the expressions of affection and support we have received," De Miguel's family said."We have been deeply moved to see so many of you rally behind this initiative."Andorra will return to action for the first time since the forward's death on Saturday when they face Almeria in the Spanish second division.

schema.headline: Jesus Owono future undecided following Jesus de Miguel death

title: What we know about Brooklyn building collapse that killed eight people
description: Figure caption, BBC's Nada Tawfik explains what we know about the Brooklyn building collapse and rescue effortsEight people have died and 18 more were
body: Figure caption, BBC's Nada Tawfik explains what we know about the Brooklyn building collapse and rescue effortsEight people have died and 18 more were injured after a three-storey building collapsed in the Flatbush neighbourhood of Brooklyn, New York.Witnesses described hearing a loud boom and seeing dust in the air as the building came down and fell into an adjacent construction pit where people were working on Wednesday. New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, described a harrowing scene, saying workers "who had only barely survived themselves turned back and dug victims out of the rubble".The city's fire commissioner, Lillian Bonsignore, said firefighters were on the scene within minutes and called their actions "incredibly heroic". Speaking on Thursday, she said fire crews "are still in a recovery phase".Despite the hard rain and falling temperatures at the site, she said, their efforts would continue until every victim was located.Image source, Getty ImagesWhere is the collapsed building?The building at 1321 Flatbush Avenue in Brooklyn was constructed in the 1930s. It contained apartments and a store.At the construction site next door, plans have been approved for a new building that will include 64 residential units and a grocery store on the bottom floor.Active work was happening on the site, and it appears part of the building fell into the construction pit, trapping and killing some workers. Why did the building collapse?It is too early to say what caused the building to collapse at around 16:00 local time (21:00 GMT) on Wednesday, but officials say they are looking into the possibility of filing criminal charges.The structure was fully occupied by residents, and construction workers were performing excavation work on a neighbouring site at the time, according to CBS News, the BBC's US partner.It's not clear if the construction had anything to do with the collapse, and the city's buildings department says it is still investigating.Investigators have said developers have active permits for excavation and foundation work associated with the new building project. The developer has been identified as Robert Fischman.In a post on X, Brooklyn District Attorney Eric Gonzalez said: "We are working closely with the Department of Buildings and our law enforcement partners to determine whether any criminal conduct contributed to this tragedy."Mayor Mamdani later emphasised this message in a news conference, saying that every entity involved in the building and the construction site will be investigated, and held accountable.Image source, Google Street View/ Getty ImagesFigure caption, Daylight shows scale of devastation after Brooklyn building collapseWho was hurt?Eight people - six adults and two children - were killed, authorities said. Two were construction workers.A further 18 people were injured.Mamdani said that six people were pronounced dead at the scene, while another two died in hospital.Four of the injured are firefighters. One person still in hospital is in a critical condition.None of the victims have yet been identified by city officials.Mamdani said they were "our friends and our neighbours. Our parents and our children. "Young families building their lives in our city, and immigrants from Mexico, Colombia, Ecuador, Trinidad and beyond."The consul general of Ecuador visited the site and confirmed that two victims are Ecuadorian nationals, the New York Times reported.Gicela Andrade told newspaper that one victim, Jose Luis Caguana Cosquillo, will be flown back to Ecuador for burial. She identified the other victim as Gabriel Ariolfo Siguencia.Image source, ReutersImage source, ReutersWhat are the conditions at the site?More than 250 firefighters responded to the collapse, working through the night to locate trapped victims.Reporters at the scene described the chaos, which occurred on a normally busy avenue of Brooklyn.The head of the NY Department of Buildings, Ahmed Tigani, said in a news conference on Thursday that there were no violations of building codes reported at the building before the collapse.He said the property developer has ties to at least 100 other sites around the city, which are also now being checked.What are the weather concerns?Forecasters predict scattered showers throughout Thursday, and then heavy rain across the New York region from 17:00 local time (22:00 GMT).The CBS meteorologist for New York, Tony Sadiku, warns there is a possibility of severe storms later in the evening, which could hamper search and recovery efforts.What did witnesses describe?One man told the BBC that he had just delivered an Amazon package to an apartment just a few minutes before the building crumbled.The man, who didn't want to share his name, described hearing a loud "boom" sound.He was shocked to see the building he had just been in reduced to rubble, he said. Within a minute or two the fire department was on the scene with several trucks, and they quickly closed the street."I live literally right behind the building", Emmanuella Carilus told the New York Times. "It sounded like a big boom and you just heard a bunch of screaming."The husband of one woman who was filmed being rescued spoke of his relief to CBS News New York."She is alive... I'm very happy. I'm very happy. I'm very happy. I thank all of you guys. She's pregnant, six months," he said.Figure caption, Video shows survivor being pulled from collapsed building in New York

schema.headline: What we know about Brooklyn building collapse that killed eight people

title: Schools, libraries and parents face 'difficult decision' over David Walliams books
description: Speaking to BBC Breakfast, Mr Di'Iasio urged the government to give schools national guidance, so they are "not leaving this open to one or two head t
body: Speaking to BBC Breakfast, Mr Di'Iasio urged the government to give schools national guidance, so they are "not leaving this open to one or two head teachers making one decision and others making a different one".Darren Morgan, head of Kings Road Primary School in Manchester, told the programme that he has taken the decision to remove Walliams' publications.The stories have been useful to promote reading, but "when there are these allegations it's really difficult to keep these books on the shelves", he said.Steve Chalke, head of Oasis Academies, which runs more than 50 schools, said it was impossible to stop children seeing the current stories about Walliams."So when a child wanders into a school and into the library and sees his name or perhaps sees his photograph on a book, it can be very traumatising for some children," he said.Author Chloe Combi, who has written about "how it feels to be young in modern Britain" and Generation Z, said banning Walliams' books is not appropriate, and could mean that important conversations about him "get swept under the carpet"."I think by talking about it and what has happened - and the responsibility of parents to have that conversation with their kids - that actually makes more sense," she told BBC Radio 5 Live."I'm totally sympathetic with schools for withdrawing him and bookshops withdrawing him as an individual decision. But the point is, none of that is going to erase what's happened."The Department for Education has been asked for comment.Retailers including Waterstones, TG Jones, and The Works, say they will no longer sell Walliams' books, and his publisher HarperCollins cut ties with him in September.Public libraries have also faced calls to remove his books.Librarians' body CILIP said it "recognises that dealing with challenges made to books or other resources can be an extremely complex and stressful situation for library staff".Decisions about stocking books are made by local councils.Among them, Kent County Council said it had no plans to remove Walliams' titles from its libraries."The starting point is that books should be available to readers unless their content is unlawful," a spokesperson said."Decisions about library stock are not made through blanket bans on individual authors. Collections are regularly reviewed and refreshed to reflect factors such as reader demand, condition and relevance of stock."A Telford and Wrekin council spokesperson added that after the "recent media coverage and allegations published in the press" they had taken the decision to "remove all Walliams' books and audio books from their library catalogues".Surrey County Council said that demand for Walliams' books had "fallen significantly in recent years", but his titles are "not illegal" and "remain available for readers to borrow".Camden Council in north London said it was putting Walliams' books in storage.A spokesperson told the Camden New Journal: "We are committed to making Camden a safer place for women and girls, to challenging harmful attitudes, and promoting healthy relationships."Following these allegations, we believe the most appropriate action is to remove these books from display."On Tuesday, ITV News and the Guardian published reports alleging that Walliams has been accused of sexual misconduct by several women, including some who accused him of "grooming" them when they were teenagers.In a letter to journalists published by the paper, Walliams said he was "not a sexual predator" and had not "broken the law".

schema.headline: Schools, libraries and parents face 'difficult decision' over David Walliams books

title: Planning permission granted for MoD Bicester asylum centre plans
description: Planning permission to house asylum seekers at a former military site near the Oxfordshire village of Piddington has been granted by the government.Th
body: Planning permission to house asylum seekers at a former military site near the Oxfordshire village of Piddington has been granted by the government.The Home Office's application to house up to 1,256 men at the MoD Bicester site was fast-tracked using an Urgent Crown Development application.The nearby village of Piddington symbolically voted to leave the UK in opposition to the planned site, which has also been legally challenged by campaigners.A Home Office spokesperson said the planning permission "allows us to continue to progress the use of MoD Bicester" but no final decision on the proposal had been taken.A government report said the decision received 3,177 representations against, and one in support.It also said Housing Secretary Angela Rayner ruled permission should be granted because "national demand for asylum accommodation remains high".The permission allows for demolition of existing buildings, the erection of new modular accommodation, and provisions for health and welfare facilities.Chris Philp MP, Shadow Home Secretary, said: "Angela Rayner and the Labour government have betrayed the people of Piddington by abusing their emergency powers in this way."He continued: "Instead of accommodating illegal immigrants, the government should leave the ECHR so they can be rapidly deported."Lib Dem MP for Bicester and Woodstock Calum Miller said it was "the wrong plan and the wrong site for local communities, asylum seekers and taxpayers"."I am deeply disappointed that the government has approved this proposal despite the serious concerns raised by residents and local councils as well as the major problems with the site," he added.The approval could be challenged by an application to the High Court within six weeks, beginning with the day after the date of the decision. The government said a challenge "may be brought only on the ground that the decision is legally flawed; it is not an opportunity to reconsider the planning merits". Joe Marshall, a Piddington parish councillor, said residents of the village were "extremely frustrated". "The government has approved its own application against more than 3,000 objections and one letter of support, overruling the councils, the NHS and the Police and Crime Commissioner," he said."No wonder we voted to leave the UK."A Home Office spokesperson said: "A final decision to proceed is yet to be taken."The government is working on a fairer distribution of asylum accommodation across the country, with over £1 billion saved in costs since the election."This includes closing all asylum hotels and moving to alternative accommodation, including former military sites. "These are designed to be self-contained, with 24/7 security and CCTV, to minimise the impact on the local community."

schema.headline: Planning permission granted for MoD Bicester asylum centre plans

title: Barcelona 1-1 Arsenal: Gritty Gunners show different side in positive draw
description: It was not a scintillating display from Arsenal, nor a tactical masterclass, but it was a gritty showing that we have not seen enough of this season.W
body: It was not a scintillating display from Arsenal, nor a tactical masterclass, but it was a gritty showing that we have not seen enough of this season.With manager Slegers under scrutiny and the players under pressure to perform, the last thing they needed was to face the full-throttle Barcelona attack.Caroline Graham Hansen's cleverness, Sydney Schertenleib's constant threat and the aura of top scorer Ewa Pajor is enough to strike fear into any team in Europe.Even with three-time Ballon d'Or winner Aitana Bonmati on the bench, Barcelona were able to impose their superiority against a wounded Arsenal – but the Gunners stood firm.Frida Maanum opened the scoring against the run of play for Arsenal in the first half and they somehow made it to half-time with their lead intact despite 18 shots from their dominant hosts.Barcelona did continue as expected after the break, equalising through Graham Hansen, but failed to kick on, with Arsenal's experience and maturity showing to see out a draw that ended the Catalan giants' 100% record in this season's Champions League."I'm very pleased in general with the players and how they have gone about it, their preparation, ownership and engagement. You know in these games it's about the margins," said Slegers."The execution was so good. It is always going to be difficult against Barcelona because they are so good on the ball. It's hard to defend against but we did well."We knew there would be opportunities. I'm really pleased with the way we played as it's very different to how we usually play. That we can do it this way [is] a big boost for us as a team."We will take that going forward because the next games are coming quickly. It is really difficult to go to Camp Nou. The one point is okay for us, though obviously we went for three."Criticism of Arsenal this season has centred around their lack of ruthlessness and an inability to turn dominance into winning results.The tables turned on Thursday as it was Barcelona who were wasteful and frustrating, while Arsenal rode their luck and capitalised where they could.Defending champions Barcelona had almost 70% possession, 24 shots, 51 touches inside the opposition half and 11 corners but only managed the solitary goal.Slegers admitted on Tuesday "too many draws" had impacted their start to the season – but was this particular draw proof that the real Arsenal is still hidden among the low confidence and poor form?"This is a very different game to play but there are of course elements in the performance that we want - and need - to take forward," added Slegers."It's there in the team and we need to show that in every single game. If you ask me what words I would use to describe the performance, I would say grit, resilience, clarity, discipline, communication, leadership and bravery as well."That is a lot of words but there were a lot of really good things in this performance that we definitely want to build on."It is a decisive few days for Arsenal with high-flying London City Lionesses up next on Sunday for a game that could impact their hopes of qualifying for next season's Champions League in the battle for a top three spot in the WSL.Then, they host French giants Lyon in Europe next Thursday before ending the league phase at Inter Milan in December.

schema.headline: Barcelona 1-1 Arsenal: Gritty Gunners show different side in positive draw

title: Man Utd's Mauricio Pochettino pursuit and Michael Carrick decisions
description: Michael Carrick must have known what was coming.Not just because reports of his imminent dismissal were widespread - followed by information about who
body: Michael Carrick must have known what was coming.Not just because reports of his imminent dismissal were widespread - followed by information about who would be replacing him as Manchester United boss.But because, effectively, he and his representatives were given heavy enough indications of what was to follow.On Monday, according to well-placed sources, Carrick's agent was contacted by chief executive Omar Berrada to be told he and director of football Jason Wilcox would be heading to Monaco for a planned meeting with co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe that would include a discussion about the head coach's future.A day later, it is believed Wilcox had a similar conversation with Carrick.It is understood that on both occasions it was communicated that a recommendation regarding Carrick's future at the club would be made.What is not clear is whether Carrick and his representatives knew that recommendation was to relieve him of his duties.By that point, BBC Sport has been told United were aware of a $10m (£7m) release clause in Mauricio Pochettino's contract with the United States national team. One source even indicated it was representatives of the Argentine who told the Premier League side.There is some regret behind the scenes at United that machinations leading to Carrick's departure on Thursday were played out so publicly.But with football clubs the size of United, keeping such developments completely private is extremely difficult - and there is a feeling they were as transparent with Carrick as they could be.Following heavy defeats by Como and Bournemouth, United placed huge importance on the following three games - against Chelsea, Roma and Aston Villa.It is understood United's leadership team were clear with Carrick that results and performances needed to improve. A defeat, a victory and draw weren't enough to save him.There is a feeling that during that three-game period, there was not enough progress, particularly in terms of team structure - underlined by the fact they conceded eight goals.Carrick has conducted himself with great dignity during the turmoil of the past few days and he leaves the club - certainly in the eyes of supporters - with his standing as a United great intact.When United first appointed Carrick - initially on an interim basis following the sacking of Ruben Amorim in January - he had a positive impact on the squad, and subsequently results.United liked his positive messaging to the players and media. They felt Carrick brought calm to rocky waters and protected his players at every opportunity - a contrast from at least the closing stages of Amorim's tenure.On the pitch, the United hierarchy felt Carrick's style of play allowed the forward players more freedom, and they won 12 of their last 17 matches of the season.While United considered other managerial options in the summer, there was ultimately a sense Carrick had earned a shot at the job on a permanent basis. The 45-year-old signed a two-year deal, though it is understood United contractually protected themselves in the event of an early termination.Part of the thought process was to provide the players with some managerial stability given the increased turnover of head coaches in recent years.Yet the season started poorly with defeat at newly promoted Hull City - and has only spiralled downward since.United are third bottom of the Premier League and 17th in the Champions League table.

schema.headline: Man Utd's Mauricio Pochettino pursuit and Michael Carrick decisions

title: Why the UK economy is surprisingly resilient
description: The UK economy grew at its fastest rate for more than two years in the three months to September."Top gear" and "strikingly strong" were among the des
body: The UK economy grew at its fastest rate for more than two years in the three months to September."Top gear" and "strikingly strong" were among the descriptions of the 0.7% growth  offered by the economists who track every minor murmur of Britain's economy.It is an upgrade on "solid" and "resilient", and in turn a world away from "hardest hit by the Iran War".Against the backdrop of the world's biggest disruption to energy flows, rising market borrowing costs - and the cruel summers since the pandemic - it is impressive growth. It should reset some of the swirl of self-reinforcing negativity. The UK's economic growth has averaged less than 0.1% in the four Q3s [ie July to September] since the pandemic. The average prediction just months ago for this July to September was just 0.1%. Even the UK's official forecaster the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) effectively pencilled in 0.3% at the Budget just 3 weeks ago. This figure has not been exceeded outside the pandemic since 2017. It puts the UK on course to be the second fastest growing economy after the US across the major G7 countries  which also includes Canada, Japan, Germany, Italy and France.It is tempting to think about what the economy would have done if the Iran War hadn't happened. If interest rates had been cut instead of their recent rise.While the latest figure kills the doom, it is clearly not a boom either. Spending on AI and tech have driven the surprise upside over the year. While the AI data centre boom may at any point turn to bust, these figures suggest that spending across the economy on investing in these technologies is helping to boost  growth. Consumers have been resilient, at least till the autumn, perhaps helped by better economic vibes.While there has been an understandable focus on high UK borrowing costs, another measure of the international standing of the UK economy, sterling's value, reached post Brexit referendum highs last week. Productivity and investment is also looking stronger, especially after recent revisions. Some of the most encouraging figures are in private sector business investment.I spoke to the chancellor at Nexeon in Oxfordshire, which is searching for a UK factory to manufacture its cutting edge electric vehicle battery - and British - technology. My colleagues visited British watchmakers in Maidenhead carving out a niche to take on the Swiss.However, this may well not last for the final three months of the year.Consumer confidence has already fallen as petrol and domestic energy prices start to rise again.There is a significant challenge with everyday cost-of-living pressures in the coming months. Construction and private house building remain depressed. The Iran conflict remains the big unknown and whether post the US midterm elections there could be a durable end to the conflict in the Gulf. Some oil and gas production there is starting to normalise. It could bring down petrol prices, energy bills, government borrowing costs, and mortgage costs too. Expect to see Downing Street investing heavily in "settlement of the conflict", which the chancellor told me is the "best economic policy".

schema.headline: Why the UK economy is surprisingly resilient

title: Two men guilty of spying for Iran over plan to target journalists and lawyer
description: Two Iranian men have been convicted of spying for an Iranian intelligence service by carrying out surveillance on journalists and a lawyer in the UK.M
body: Two Iranian men have been convicted of spying for an Iranian intelligence service by carrying out surveillance on journalists and a lawyer in the UK.Mostafa Sepahvand, 41, and Farhad Javadi Manesh, 46, were convicted of "assisting a foreign intelligence service" at Woolwich Crown Court on Thursday.They were tasked by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) with monitoring the targets. Sepahvand intended to carry out a "violent attack" against at least one of them, while Manesh helped with planning.A third man, Shapoor Qalehali Khani Noori, 57, was cleared of the same charge.Sepahvand was in contact with two men with Iranian telephone numbers.Police seized 534GB of data that showed Sapahvand and Manesh were given documents that included pictures of targets, their work addresses, the make and colour of their cars and the names of pets. They then used ChatGPT to carry out further research.The pair, from west London, are asylum seekers who had been granted temporary leave to remain. Sepahvand arrived in the UK in a lorry in 2016, and Manesh arrived via small boat in 2019.Sepahvand conducted surveillance and reconnaissance in preparation for inflicting violence on several "subjects" in the UK.These included journalists Mojtaba Pourmohsen and Kambiz Hosseini, who worked for the London-based Persian broadcaster Iran international, Jonathan Turner, a founding member of UK Lawyers for Israel, as well as a media production professional.Deputy Assistant Commissioner Vicki Evans, the senior national co-ordinator for Counter-Terrorism Policing, said it was the first time ChatGPT case search history had been presented in a state threat case.She added: "It's something we're beginning to see more of as AI tools become more widely available and people become more aware of them."It was clear from the evidence at the trial that at times Sepahvand felt he was being mistreated by his Iranian handlers, who had not paid him.Evans said: "This is a trend we see in these types of cases where people get involved in work on behalf of foreign states and they're often promised money and lots of other things but they rarely receive what they've been offered."Sepahvand had claimed he participated in the spying out of fear of the consequences of refusing but the prosecution described this as "entirely bogus".In voice notes sent to an Iranian contact, he said he had been promised that a conviction for theft in Iran would be "sorted out" - which prosecutors said was part of his motivation for conducting the surveillance.Sepahvand also asked for £150,000 in exchange for "finishing off" a target, stressing that he would "do it".Frank Ferguson, of the Crown Prosecution Service's counter-terrorism division, said the two men had been promised rewards for sending intelligence back to contacts in Iran."Sepahvand himself was willing to go beyond surveillance to commit serious violence against their targets," he said."Thankfully, the defendants were stopped before any attack could take place."Cases like this show Iranian intelligence's willingness to use proxies to target the regime's critics abroad."A spokesperson for Iran International said the verdicts would not "make the lives of our journalists any safer so long as the Islamic Republic of Iran continues its campaign of death threats and violence against them". A statement continued: "Kambiz Hosseini and Mojtaba Pourmohsen and others remain under threat. "We are thankful for the continued vigilance of the British police in protecting not only us but the many other Iranians targeted by Iran. "Iran will no doubt continue its use of agents and proxies abroad in its campaign to terrorise its critics."Sepahvand and Manesh will be sentenced at the Old Bailey on 17 December.Additional reporting by Ghoncheh Habibiazad

title: Can Andy Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?
description: Andy Burnham has committed to bringing the welfare bill down, but he knows just how the high the political stakes are.He saw how last year's welfare r
body: Andy Burnham has committed to bringing the welfare bill down, but he knows just how the high the political stakes are.He saw how last year's welfare rebellion marked the beginning of the end for his predecessor in Downing Street.Sir Keir Starmer's authority was shredded when 120 - more than a quarter - of his own MPs threatened to derail his reforms.To defuse this, Sir Keir was compelled to guarantee that existing claimants of personal independence payment (Pip), the main disability benefit in England and Wales, wouldn't lose out.Even then, 49 of the 120 potential Labour rebels still voted against their own government.Next week, a review from former New Labour cabinet minister Alan Milburn has the capacity to create another internal row in Labour's ranks.  Milburn has spent a year grappling with how to reduce the nearly one million young people who are not in employment, education or training (Neets).In an interview with the Times, he has now confirmed he is set to recommend cutting benefits for some 16-24 year olds who currently receive Pip, or the enhanced health-related payment of Universal Credit.Taking benefit cuts to the Parliamentary Labour Party would usually have a similar effect to adding phosphorous to water.But from my soundings, the deep waters of the Labour ranks are calmer than might be expected.Why? Importantly, two of the most effective organisers of last year's welfare rebellion are batting for the current prime minister, rather than against the previous one. Louise Haigh is now the most powerful cabinet minister after Andy Burnham himself, while Anneliese Midgeley is his chief whip. And the MP who fronted that rebellion - Meg Hillier - has said she wants to give Milburn's proposals a "fair wind".There are also clear differences to the previous approach to welfare reform. First, it is not being presented as primarily a cost-cutting exercise with pre-determined savings. Instead, there will be upfront investment to provide more support to unemployed young people, and a timeframe for net savings likely to be set at around a decade – gradualism, not a short, sharp shock.Second, last year's initial reforms would have affected people in all age groups, whilst benefit cuts this time would be limited to the under 25s, who make up around 11% of Pip claimants.I've spoken to government ministers who had expressed concerns – at least privately – about the changes devised previously by Rachel Reeves and Liz Kendall.  This time, they are on board.One of them told me that so long as there was enough support for young people, with guaranteed jobs and training, MPs would be "fine" with some benefit cuts.But they added that it was vital that those who really couldn't work wouldn't be worse off. Milburn will suggest there could even be enhanced payments for people in this category, while some young people with disabilities who lose out on Pip could nonetheless be given an additional "allowance" to help with living costs.Another minister who opposed the previous reforms praised the process this time. There had been a high level of engagement not just from Milburn, but Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden, who has been taking MPs through the principles behind the reforms.One minister was a little more cautious, suggesting support for a reduction in benefits would depend on what the entire "package" of reforms looked like. Milburn's recommendations are likely to be wide-ranging – from pre-school policies to how the NHS deals with mental health.Some of the eventual 49 rebels from last year are in a similar place. York MP Rachael Maskell told me it was essential that she saw the detail of the proposals rather than the "drip, drip" of press reports which would "cause young people stress and distress".She felt withdrawing Pip from young people was "like a sledgehammer to crack a nut" and was concerned that some disabled people required it to remain in work. She also suggested that the government "shouldn't just point the finger at young people," and should look closely at how employers could take more youngsters on.Stroud MP Simon Opher also voted against the government on welfare last year. He told me there was a "crisis" with so many Neets, and Milburn had come up with a "credible solution".But he believes cutting benefits should be a "last resort" and is worried about restricting access to the health element of Universal Credit, as a quarter of young claimants aren't Neet. He concludes that the "devil will be in the detail".So much of politics - like comedy – depends on timing.For some sceptics, including serving ministers, the Milburn proposals will be more warmly welcomed if support for young people is in place before entitlements are withdrawn.But for some Labour MPs, cutting payments to existing claimants crosses a line.Clapham and Brixton Hill MP Bell Ribiero-Addy has she wasn't sure she could back cuts.Referring to Pip, she didn't believe that "you get a disabled young person into work by taking away the money that helps them to get into work".And another MP on the left of the party, Brian Leishman, told the BBC he couldn't back benefits cuts as "we are in the middle of a cost of living crisis".So a welfare rebellion seems guaranteed if Burnham accepts Milburn's recommendations.But it seems unlikely to be of the same scale, or have a similar level of political jeopardy to the one which shook the Starmer government.

title: Hegseth awards medal to war memorial guard who reprimanded him and group
description: Figure caption, US Army guard reprimands group that includes US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth at Arlington National Cemetery.ByGrace Eliza GoodwinUpd
body: Figure caption, US Army guard reprimands group that includes US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth at Arlington National Cemetery.ByGrace Eliza GoodwinUpdated 3 hours agoUS Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has awarded a medal to the guard who reprimanded his group at Arlington National Cemetery.A video of a Veterans Day observance event on Wednesday showed Hegseth, his wife, and senior advisers laughing and talking while posing for photos in front of the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier before the guard told them to be quiet. In a statement, the Pentagon later announced that Hegseth had given Specialist Thomas Iglesias a Joint Service Commendation Medal "for the execution of his duties at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier".Photos shared on the defence secretary's X account showed him presenting the medal to Iglesias.He was accompanied by others whom the Pentagon identified as members of the 3rd US Infantry Regiment, known as the Old Guard, which is responsible for holding vigil over the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. "We love soldiers. We love standards. Well done, Specialist. Carry on Patriots," the accompanying text on Hegseth's post reads. In the video, the army sentinel on duty later identified as Iglesias can be seen stepping towards Hegseth's group and shouting: "All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times."Image source, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth/XImage caption, Hegseth (right) awarded the medal to Specialist Thomas Iglesias after being reprimanded by himThe Arlington National Cemetery etiquette requests that visitors speak quietly and do not engage in disrespectful or disorderly conduct. The tomb, which is one of the country's most sacred war memorials, marks the final resting place of an unknown soldier who was killed in World War I. Chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell later said in a statement: "While commemorating this solemn day, a soldier correctly and respectfully reminded everyone to maintain decorum.""The Secretary and the entire Department have always honoured - and will always honour - the sacrifices our military men and women have made to keep America safe." A service member from the 3rd Infantry Regiment stands watch over the tomb 24 hours a day and has done so since 1948.It is not unusual for them to admonish visitors to the site, according to the BBC's US partner CBS News. They reportedly do so a few times a day.Image source, AFP via Getty ImagesImage caption, Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and First Lady Melania Trump bow their heads in prayer during a Veterans Day ceremony at Arlington National Cemetery Earlier, President Donald Trump, Vice-President JD Vance and other top officials attended the annual wreath-laying ceremony at the cemetery.During his speech at the ceremony, Trump offered his gratitude to uniformed service members who have fought for the country. He also touted what he sees as his administration's success in the Iran war."Under this administration, and it was about time, somebody fought back. All of us fought back," he said. "And we won," Trump said of the Iran war. "It's just a question of when we want to end it. We want to make sure we have a total victory, not a 93% victory."Trump also pointed out Hegseth during the ceremony, saying he's done a "fantastic job" as defence secretary. Trump has repeatedly defended Hegseth amid Democratic lawmakers' push to impeach him. On Tuesday, an effort to impeach the defence secretary under accusations that he waged war on Iran without congressional authorisation failed on Capitol Hill.Hegseth has called the impeachment efforts a "farce" and a "stunt".

title: England vs Croatia player ratings: Harry Kane scores winner as Lewis Hall impresses
description: Jordan Pickford - Was left exposed by Jarell Quansah's mistake for Croatia's goal. Was as reliable as ever prior to that. 6Trent Alexander-Arnold - Pl
body: Jordan Pickford - Was left exposed by Jarell Quansah's mistake for Croatia's goal. Was as reliable as ever prior to that. 6Trent Alexander-Arnold - Played within himself. Some nice link-up play with Morgan Rogers down the right. 6Jarell Quansah - Dreadful mistake to gift Croatia an equaliser. Was entirely comfortable up to that point. 5Dan Burn - Not picked in the original squad but started. Unspectacular but largely reliable in the heart of defence. 6Lewis Hall - Another effective contribution from the Newcastle defender. Is he now England's first-choice left-back? 7Elliot Anderson - Kept things ticking over nicely in the engine room and always looked to play forward. 6Declan Rice - Back in the team after missing the previous internationals through injury and conducted the midfield expertly. 6Jude Bellingham - Not quite the outstanding level as his most recent England displays but still oozed quality in possession. 6Morgan Rogers - Posed a threat down the right and deserved his goal - his third for England at senior level. 6Harry Kane - A historic night for the England captain as he became the nation's most capped player. Scored the winner from the spot to boot. 6Anthony Gordon - Was sensational during the last set of international games. Less so here, but remains crucial for England. 6Substitutes Rio Ngumoha (on for Gordon 78). 6Ben White (on for Alexander-Arnold 78). 6James Garner (on for Garner 78). 6Subs not used: Trafford, Steele, Gibbs-White, Hill, Branthwaite, Jobe Bellingham, Calvert-Lewin, Eze, King
